text: Meanwhile, the first stranger quietly returned to the empty cottage, and soon the hangman came back too, so the two ate and drank together before parting. <break time="0.8s" /> Out on the hills, the searchers at last found the little man standing quietly near a tree, and he calmly allowed himself to be taken back. <break time="0.8s" /> But at the cottage, two officers from the jail looked at him and declared that this was not the escaped prisoner at all, but a completely different man. <break time="0.8s" /> The little man then explained that he was the prisoners brother, who had been walking to Casterbridge to see him for the last time. <break time="0.8s" /> When he had looked into the cottage and seen his brother sitting beside the hangman, he had been so shocked that he could only run away. <break time="0.8s" /> Only then did everyone realize that the quiet man by the fire, who had sung so cheerfully with the hangman, had been the escaped prisoner himself. <break time="0.8s" /> The search went on for days, but the country people pitied the poor man, so he was never caught, and his story is still told in Wessex today. <break time="0.8s" /> Shepherd Fennel and his wife have long since died, and the baby whose christening they celebrated that night is now a woman growing old herself.
